## Overview

Authenticated rate limits use a server-side reputation layer. It scores users,
sessions, API keys and network origins from auditable signals, then returns a
coarse risk tier and a rate-limit multiplier to the API and database guards.
Trusted, organic use gets more headroom; suspicious automation gets less.

- The policy runs only on the server. Scoring rules and reason codes are never
  sent to clients or shown in responses.
- Request-shape signals can raise caution; they cannot earn trust on their own.
- Sensitive actions can require a fresh step-up verification tied to the same
  session.
- People who are rate limited can appeal, and operators can investigate with
  audit records.

Operational detail for these controls is maintained internally and is not published, because this repository is open source and published thresholds or rejection rules would help attackers.
